body.statement: There are constants depending only on \((c_-,c_+,\kappa,\lambda_0)\) such that, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n\) and \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), \(P\{e(X)\le\lambda\}\asymp\lambda^{\kappa}\) and \(E_P[(e(X)\vee\lambda)^{-1}]\asymp v_{\kappa}(\lambda)^2\), where \(v_{\kappa}(\lambda)=\lambda^{-(1-\kappa)/2}\) for \(0<\kappa<1\), \(v_1(\lambda)=\sqrt{1+\log(\lambda_0/\lambda)}\), and \(v_{\kappa}(\lambda)=1\) for \(\kappa>1\).
body.justification: This converts the primitive dyadic law into the two uniform tail functionals used on both sides of the frontier.
body.gap: KhanTamer2010Irregular gives tail-rate intuition but not this class-uniform dyadic-shell equivalence.
body.consumer: The clipped-score upper bound and every shell-localized lower family use these uniform comparisons.
